memory_verse.text: "You are the light of the world. A town built on a hill cannot be hidden." — Matthew 5:14

devotion.label: Insight / Reflection
devotion.text:
The reaction of India to the Christian Gospel has gone through three stages: 
(1) It isn’t true. 
(2) It isn’t new. 
(3) It isn’t you. 

The first stage was short-lived. The Gospel was so self-verifying to the human mind that it could not be waved out as untrue. The second stage, “It isn’t new,” has lingered and is still in vogue “Everything you have in your faith is found in our sacred books.” The third stage, “It isn’t you”, “You don’t live it’ is here and is the usual argument against the Christian Gospel. 
Most seriously last point is more important "Yes we didn't live it". The truth is exclamatory. we have to live according to the truth we proclaim. 
The history of the Gospel in India reveals a profound shift from questioning the message to questioning the messenger. While many may claim the Gospel "isn't new" pointing to ancient "shadows" in their own traditions the most piercing critique remains: "It isn’t you." This is not a rejection of Christ, but a challenge to those who bear His name. If the Truth is truly exclamatory and life-changing, it must be visible in our character.

quote.label: Today's Quote
quote.text: "The greatest single cause of atheism in the world today is Christians: who acknowledge Jesus with their lips, walk out the door, and deny Him by their lifestyle." — Brennan Manning

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, forgive us for the times our lives have been a stumbling block to Your Truth. We acknowledge that while the Gospel is perfect, we have often failed to mirror Your heart. Strip away the hypocrisy and the hollow words. Help us to move beyond "proclaiming" the light to actually "being" the light. Let our actions be so aligned with Your Word that others see You in us. Amen.

conclusion.label: A Word to You
text: Today, remember that you are the only Bible some people will ever read. The world isn't looking for a better argument; it’s looking for a better life. Don't just tell them the Gospel is true show them it is real.
